headline: Biman to purchase 10 Airbus aircraft to expand fleet
summary: The government announced the acquisition of four wide-body A350-900s and six narrow-body A321neo aircraft to meet passenger demand.
details: The government has announced plans to purchase 10 Airbus aircraft for Biman Bangladesh Airlines, with the deal expected to be finalized in October.
Civil Aviation and Tourism Minister M Rashiduzzaman Millat announced the decision at a press briefing on Tuesday, stating that the move is driven by passenger demand.
The order consists of four wide-body Airbus A350-900s and six narrow-body A321neo aircraft.
This purchase follows previous agreements to acquire 25 Boeing aircraft, including 14 in April and 11 in September.
With the latest Airbus announcement, Biman is set to add a total of 35 new aircraft to its fleet through planned purchases from both Boeing and Airbus.
The decision comes amid diplomatic pressure from France and other European countries, with the French Ambassador to Dhaka previously describing the deal as a 'test' for the current government.
The proposal for the Airbus purchase originated from a pledge made during French President Emmanuel Macron's visit to Dhaka in September 2023.
caption:
Biman is set to add 35 new planes to its fleet! ✈️

Government announces the purchase of 10 Airbus jets to meet growing passenger demand.

The government has announced plans to purchase 10 Airbus aircraft for Biman Bangladesh Airlines, with the deal expected to be finalized in October.

Civil Aviation and Tourism Minister M Rashiduzzaman Millat announced the decision at a press briefing on Tuesday, stating that the move is driven by passenger demand.

The order consists of four wide-body Airbus A350-900s and six narrow-body A321neo aircraft.

This purchase follows previous agreements to acquire 25 Boeing aircraft, including 14 in April and 11 in September.

With the latest Airbus announcement, Biman is set to add a total of 35 new aircraft to its fleet through planned purchases from both Boeing and Airbus.

The decision comes amid diplomatic pressure from France and other European countries, with the French Ambassador to Dhaka previously describing the deal as a 'test' for the current government.

The proposal for the Airbus purchase originated from a pledge made during French President Emmanuel Macron's visit to Dhaka in September 2023.

headline_marked: Local govt elections to [[begin in January and end by June 6]]
headline: Local govt elections to begin in January and end by June 6
summary: State Minister Mir Shahe Alam says the government is committed to ensuring a free, fair, and neutral election process.
details: State Minister for Local Government, Rural Development and Co-operatives Mir Shahe Alam announced that local government elections will start in January and conclude by June 6.
Speaking at a law and order meeting in Rangpur, the minister stated that these dates are based on information from the Election Commission.
He emphasized that the government is determined to conduct a free, fair, and neutral election, ensuring that there is no 'tainted chapter' in the process.
Beyond elections, the minister revealed that 127 crore BDT has been allocated for road repairs and development in Rangpur district over the last six months.
A new project worth 3,600 crore BDT for infrastructure development in Rangpur, Lalmonirhat, Kurigram, and Nilphamari districts has been sent to ECnec for approval.
Additional projects for public health and municipal development in the Rangpur division are also in the pipeline.
The minister also mentioned plans for region-based crop prioritization through 'zone maps' to boost the agricultural sector.
Regarding the Teesta project, the minister confirmed that the government is working on the comprehensive plan and will implement it soon.
caption:
Local government elections are set to begin in January and wrap up by June 6, according to State Minister Mir Shahe Alam.

State Minister for Local Government, Rural Development and Co-operatives Mir Shahe Alam announced that local government elections will start in January and conclude by June 6.

Speaking at a law and order meeting in Rangpur, the minister stated that these dates are based on information from the Election Commission.

He emphasized that the government is determined to conduct a free, fair, and neutral election, ensuring that there is no 'tainted chapter' in the process.

Beyond elections, the minister revealed that 127 crore BDT has been allocated for road repairs and development in Rangpur district over the last six months.

A new project worth 3,600 crore BDT for infrastructure development in Rangpur, Lalmonirhat, Kurigram, and Nilphamari districts has been sent to ECnec for approval.

Additional projects for public health and municipal development in the Rangpur division are also in the pipeline.

The minister also mentioned plans for region-based crop prioritization through 'zone maps' to boost the agricultural sector.

Regarding the Teesta project, the minister confirmed that the government is working on the comprehensive plan and will implement it soon.
